gaps.sentence: She works as ___ waitress during the summer holidays.
gaps.explanation: After 'as' and 'work as', jobs take a/an: work as a waitress.

gaps.sentence: ___ United Kingdom consists of four countries.
gaps.explanation: 'The United Kingdom', 'the USA', 'the Czech Republic' all take 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He is ___ most experienced teacher in the school.
gaps.explanation: Superlative + of/in-phrase: the most experienced teacher in the school.
'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

gaps.sentence: ___ good news is that sales are up by twenty per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'News' is uncountable but takes 'the' when specified: the good news is… 'Sales' here is general, so no article.

gaps.sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
gaps.explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.

gaps.sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He earns fifty thousand pounds ___ year.
gaps.explanation: 'Fifty thousand a year' — 'a' = per in rates.
